title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy — Password reset poisoning
claim: Documents password reset poisoning: an attacker manipulates a vulnerable website into generating a password-reset link pointing to a domain under their control, by controlling the Host header used to construct that link; attributes original documentation of the technique to 2013 research by PortSwigger's Director of Research.

title: IETF RFC 9112 — HTTP/1.1
claim: Specifies request-target forms (origin-form, absolute-form, authority-form, asterisk-form); requires that when a request-target is in absolute-form, an origin server MUST ignore any received Host header field and use the request-target's host information instead; requires a client to still send a Host header field even in this case for compatibility with older HTTP/1.0 proxies.

title: Django Security Advisory (via FreeBSD portaudit) — Host header poisoning
claim: Documents that Django's django.http.HttpRequest.get_host() in the affected versions incorrectly handled userinfo-style syntax in the Host header (e.g. 'validsite.com:random@evilsite.com'), allowing an attacker-controlled domain to be accepted and used, particularly by the password-reset mechanism, to generate arbitrary URLs.
